title.value: Intervertebral Disc Labeling With Learning Shape Information, A Look Once Approach
title.justification: The title accurately captures the primary focus of the paper, which is about a novel approach for intervertebral disc labeling using deep learning techniques that incorporate shape information.
title.quote: Intervertebral Disc Labeling With Learning Shape Information, A Look Once Approach

extractions.description: The paper presents a novel U-Net-based architecture for the automatic segmentation of intervertebral discs in medical images, aimed at improving the diagnosis of spine-related diseases. The method incorporates shape information to enhance model performance and introduces a 'look once' model for efficient disc location prediction, reducing false positives. Evaluated on a publicly available dataset, the approach demonstrated superior performance over existing methods.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on medical image segmentation for spine-related disease diagnosis, which does not directly relate to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Accurate and automatic segmentation of intervertebral discs from medical images is a critical task for the assessment of spine-related diseases such as osteoporosis, vertebral fractures, and intervertebral disc herniation.

primary_category.quote: To date, various approaches have been developed in the literature which routinely rely on detecting the discs as the primary step.

primary_sub_category.quote: In this study, we aim to allevi-ate this problem by proposing a novel U-Net-based structure to predict a set of candidates for intervertebral disc locations.

new_primary_category.quote: Our proposed method consists of two stages. In the first stage we utilize a U-Net-based structure to detect and predict semantic labeling for each intervertebral disc location.

new_primary_sub_category.quote: The main idea is that, inspired by the idea of YOLO [23], we propose a permutation invariant ’look once’ model to increase the True Positive (TP) rate while reducing the FN detection.
